    StartersMainsSweetsDrinks
    StartersEmerald City pea and mint soupBright green pea and mint soup with a swirl of creamHow to make it30g butter1 onion, diced1 garlic clove, crushed750g frozen peas1 L vegetable stock1 mint100ml thickened creamSoften the onion and garlic in the butter for 6 minutes.Add the stock and bring to the boil, then the peas, and simmer 4 minutes.Add most of the mint leaves and blend until smooth and very green. Season.Serve with a swirl of cream and the rest of the mint.Munchkinland cheese strawsTwisted puff pastry straws with cheddar, parmesan and paprikaHow to make it2 sheets of frozen puff pastry, thawed1 egg, beaten80g vintage cheddar, finely grated40g parmesan, finely grated1 tsp sweet paprikaHeat the oven to 200°C and line two trays.Brush one pastry sheet with egg, scatter with the cheeses and paprika, and lay the second sheet on top. Press down.Cut into 1.5cm strips and twist each one.Bake 12 to 14 minutes until puffed and golden. Cool on the trays.MainsKansas farm fried chickenButtermilk soaked drumsticks in paprika flour, fried crisp, with mashHow to make it8 chicken drumsticks500ml buttermilk200g plain flour2 tsp smoked paprika1kg potatoes50g butter500ml chicken stock1 L vegetable oil, for fryingsalt, to tasteSoak the drumsticks in buttermilk in the fridge overnight.Rest the chicken in the buttermilk.Peel and boil the potatoes, then mash with butter.Dredge the chicken in flour seasoned with paprika and salt.Fry in the vegetable oil at 170°C in batches until crisp and cooked through.Simmer the stock with a little flour to make a gravy and serve with the mash.Emerald City pesto penne with broccoliGreen pesto penne and broccoli, Emerald City styleHow to make itAs written, serves 4Penne cooked with broccoli and peas in the same pot, tossed with basil pesto, parmesan and lemon until bright green.Cook 400g penne in salted water, adding 1 head broccoli in small florets and 1 cup frozen peas for the last 3 minutes.Drain, keeping a cup of the water.Toss with 190g basil pesto, the zest and juice of 1 lemon and 50g grated parmesan, adding pasta water until glossy.Toast 40g pine nuts in a dry pan.Serve topped with the pine nuts, extra parmesan and a handful of basil leaves.SweetsRuby slipper jellyRaspberry jelly in glasses. Tap your heels three times.How to make it1 packet raspberry jelly crystals125g raspberries1 tsp edible glitter150ml thickened creamMake up the jelly as the packet says.Divide the raspberries between four glasses and pour the jelly over.Chill until set.Whip the cream, dust the jellies with glitter and top with cream.Fried choux crullersTwisted rings of choux, just fried, says Auntie EmHow to make it250ml water100g butter150g plain flour4 eggs1 L vegetable oil, for frying150g icing sugar2 tbsp honey2 tbsp full cream milkCut squares of baking paper and bring the water and butter to the boil.Beat in the flour until a smooth ball forms, cool slightly, then beat in the eggs one at a time.Pipe twisted rings onto the paper squares.Fry in oil at 180°C, paper and all, until golden, peeling the paper off once they float.Mix the icing sugar, honey and milk into a glaze and dip the warm crullers.Lollipop Guild lollipopsHard boiled sugar lollipops tinted in two coloursHow to make it200g caster sugar80ml glucose syrup80ml water1 tsp food colouring, two colours1 packet lollipop sticksLine trays with baking paper.Boil the sugar, glucose and water to 150°C without stirring.Split between two small pans, tint each a different colour with the food colouring and pour small rounds onto the paper, swirling the colours.Press a stick into each and leave to harden.Grumpy tree salted caramel applesCaramel apple wedges. Ask the angry tree first.How to make itAs written, serves 4Crisp red apple wedges with a warm salted caramel dip, crushed roasted peanuts and a dusting of cinnamon for dunking.Melt 100g brown sugar with 60g butter, stirring for 2 minutes, then pour in 125ml cream and simmer 3 minutes until thick.Take off the heat and stir in half a teaspoon of salt.Cut 4 red apples into wedges and toss in lemon juice so they don't brown.Pour the warm caramel into a bowl, scatter with 60g crushed roasted peanuts and a pinch of cinnamon and serve with the apples.DrinksYellow brick road pineapple lemonadeLemon, pineapple and ginger. Follow the road.How to make it80g caster sugar80ml water1 tsp grated ginger4 lemons400ml pineapple juice400ml soda water1/4 pineapple1 bag iceSimmer the sugar, water and ginger for 2 minutes, then cool and strain.Juice the lemons and mix with the syrup and pineapple juice.Fill four tall glasses with ice, share the mix between them and top with soda water.Finish each with a pineapple wedge on the rim.
